title: LLMulator: Generalizable Cost Modeling for Dataflow Accelerators with Input-Adaptive Control Flow
problem: Existing performance prediction methods for dataflow-based accelerators (TPUs, NPUs, FPGAs) fail to generalize across three dimensions: unseen applications with extreme loop scales (errors exceeding 40%), input-dependent control flows where branch probabilities shift at runtime (errors up to 60%), and diverse hardware architectures with varying memory delays and loop mapping primitives. No prior method unifies all three generalization axes.
motivation: Accurate, fast cost modeling is the critical bottleneck in design-space exploration for dataflow accelerators, and the growing complexity of hardware-software stacks (HLS, spatial mappings, dynamic operators) makes hand-crafted analytical models and static graph neural network approaches obsolete.
method: LLMulator uses a pre-trained LLM (LLaMA-3.2-1B fine-tuned via LoRA) as the backbone for cost prediction with three novel mechanisms: (1) Progressive numeric encoding that tokenizes each decimal digit independently and uses categorical cross-entropy rather than regression to predict performance as digit-wise classification with beam-search error correction, enabling range-agnostic estimates; (2) Dynamic Prediction Calibration (DPC) using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)-style reinforcement learning with a replay buffer, where the model is updated online from Verilator simulation feedback to adapt to runtime input variations in loop bounds and control-flow branching; (3) A progressive dataset synthesizer that generates multi-level training data via AST-based generation, dataflow-specific loop-tree mutation, and LLM-based augmentation, then formats data with intermediate RTL reasoning chains (via SiliconCompiler and OpenROAD) to teach the model compilation-level reasoning.
key_novelty: Treating hardware performance values as digit-wise categorical token sequences (rather than regression targets) enables confidence-aware, range-agnostic prediction that generalizes to out-of-distribution loop scales, combined with RL-based online calibration for input-adaptive control flows.
contributions: Progressive numeric modeling paradigm that tokenizes numerical program values digit-by-digit with categorical output and beam search, reducing edge-value prediction errors by 2.3%–13.6% over regression baselines.

Dynamic Prediction Calibration framework using DPO-based reinforcement learning from simulation feedback, converging to 11.2% cycle prediction error after a few iterations, a 9.7% improvement over static models.

Progressive data augmentation framework combining AST generation, dataflow-specific loop mutation, and LLM self-augmentation, with hardware mapping parameters (memory delays, loop unroll pragmas) to cover diverse hardware configs.
End-to-end LLMulator framework achieving 12.2% MAPE on ASIC design scenarios, reducing error by 16.7%–7.8% compared to GNNHLS and TLP state-of-the-art methods.

metrics.accuracy: 12.2% MAPE on ASIC scenarios; 9.7% error reduction from DPC over static; 16.7%–7.8% error reduction vs GNNHLS/TLP

limitations: Calibration via DPO requires repeated simulation runs (Verilator) per input, adding profiling overhead that may be prohibitive for very large dataflow programs; the method targets HLS-level (C-to-RTL) modeling and does not address post-place-and-route variability.
primary_theme: LLM-based generalizable cost modeling for dataflow accelerators
